_doc: Direct score-delta happy path: POST /api/brand/score-delta scores a before URL and an after URL and returns the before/after delta in one call. Deterministic (no LLM, no worker) — ungated, green as soon as analysis_service is deployed. Exercises fetch+score on BOTH sides plus the pure compute_score_deltas/compare_findings core. Asserts stable keys overall_delta + score_deltas (always set on a 200), never volatile per-finding output.
_assertions: CLOSED 2026-09-06 by the engine change in scripts/e2e_validate.py: run_service_probe now desugars `expect_keys` into STRICT `present` checks (0/0.0/False/[]/{}/"" all FAIL) and accepts a `checks` list evaluated by the same _eval_check used by expect_stage_assertions. The discriminating floors below are what make this probe fail on a response that fetched or scored nothing.
_overall_delta_is_not_a_presence_check: `overall_delta` is deliberately NOT in expect_keys: presence is now STRICT (falsy fails) and a delta of exactly 0.0 is LEGITIMATE (identical before/after scores). It is asserted instead as `numeric_gte overall_delta >= -100`. That bound is NOT a meaningful floor - no numerically valid delta of two 0-100 scores can fail it; it is a type/presence guard that rejects a null, a non-numeric, or an absent key without reddening an honest zero. The discriminating power for this scenario lives in the before/after numeric_gte and nonempty checks below, not here.
